title: Until Powerhouse supports Artifact editing, Launch Agent 7 amendments are enacted as GitHub pull requests against the Atlas repository
content:
Two Short-Term Transitionary Measures reveal the gap between the specified system and the operating one. On submission (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1): until Powerhouse supports Artifact Edit Proposals, holders post to the Sky Forum under the "Launch Agent 7 Prime" category with a title containing "Launch Agent 7 Artifact Edit Proposal" and "cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage." On enactment (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.5.1): the Operational Facilitator "works with the Core Facilitator to update the Atlas GitHub repository located at https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pulls to reflect proposals approved by Prime Governance."

The substantive point is that the Artifact's authoritative store is presently a git repository, and writing to it requires two named human roles acting together — including the **Core Facilitator**, an ecosystem-level actor who appears nowhere else in Launch Agent 7's routine protocol. In the interim, ecosystem-level cooperation is a hard dependency for any Agent-level amendment.

The forum-plus-signature workaround is the more interesting substitution: it replaces a system-enforced eligibility check with a manually verified cryptographic attestation. Eligibility becomes something a reader must verify rather than something the process guarantees.

This is worth flagging as a live discrepancy rather than a defect: the specified process (Powerhouse, automated) and the practised process (Forum, GitHub, manual) coexist in the same document, and the Artifact is explicit that the latter is temporary scaffolding.
description: Transitionary measures route proposals through Sky Forum posts with cryptographic proof of holdings, and enactment through the Operational Facilitator working with the Core Facilitator on GitHub.
